title: Terry v. Ohio (1968)
key_points: Holding: Police may briefly stop a person on reasonable, articulable suspicion of criminal activity, and may frisk outer clothing for weapons if they reasonably suspect the person is armed and dangerous.
officer_notes: Scenario: You watch two men take turns walking past a jewelry store window a dozen times and conferring at the corner. You stop them to ask questions.
Takeaway: Write down the specific facts that made you suspicious; a hunch is not enough.
